title: Circuit-breaker fractional rollouts — lab notes
notes:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for a run that mixes fractional rollouts (percent-based routing to fallback/premium models) with an adaptive circuit-breaker that trips on token-timeouts and p99 latency spikes. Trying to capture config knobs, a few raw results, and an emergent behaviour that might explain tail amplification under mixed-priority traffic.

Context:
- Problem: when a fraction of traffic is routed to cheaper quantized variants (for cost savings) we sometimes see the p99 of the premium path jump unexpectedly after transient load spikes. Hypothesis: the fraction routing + per-tenant circuit-breaker/backpressure interplay creates a feedback loop (route more to premium when fallback degrades, premium then overloads, trips breaker, bulk rerouted, oscillation).
- Goal: reproduce reliably in a small synthetic replay, then propose safe heuristics.

Experiment setup (replay):
- Workload source: local replay harness (replay/mini-replay v0.9) using production A/B ingress trace (sanitized) sampling 15m window.
- Traffic pattern: 10k concurrent connections simulated, overall 350 qps nominal, 3s on/off microbursts every 90s to stress warm caches.
- Model variants:
  - premium: llama-70b-fp16 (high-perf; pinned to premium pool)
  - cheap: quant-7b-4bit (fast-ish; larger burst capacity)
- Routing policy: fractional_rollout_percent = 30% -> cheap, 70% -> premium.
- Circuit-breaker policy (new adaptive):
  - measure_window = 30s, trip_condition = p99 > 800ms OR error_rate > 0.8%
  - cooldown = 45s, half-open_probe = 5 concurrent requests, ramp-back = linear over cooldown
  - override: maintain minimum premium_capacity = 10 qps (avoid full starvation)
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency (end-to-end), per-model queue length, GPU util %, per-tenant circuit state transitions, kv-cache hit rate.

Commands run (notes):
- started with: ./replay --trace sample15m.json --qps 350 --burst-schedule="3s:0/90s" --concurrency 10000 --policy=frac:30
- runtime flags: --cb-mode=adaptive --cb-window=30s --cb-p99-threshold=800ms --min-premium-qps=10

Raw observations (timeline):
- 00:00–02:30 (steady): premium p99 ~ 320ms; cheap p99 ~ 210ms; overall p95 ~ 120ms. GPU util premium ~ 46%. kv-cache hit 74%. No circuit trips.
- 02:30 burst 0–3s: small microburst (simulated) — cheap path latency drops (due to burst capacity) but premium p99 rises to ~580ms for 15s after burst as premium queues backfill. CB remained closed.
- 05:40 second stronger burst: premium p99 spikes to ~980ms for 22s -> CB trips (state->open) at 05:43. Observed immediate +18% routing shift to cheap (policy respects fractional but CB overrides by offloading some tenants).
- 05:43–06:30 chaotic period: premium drops to minimal traffic; cheap handles bulk -> cheap GPU util jumps to 90%, cheap p99 grows from 210ms to 480ms over 30s due to increased concurrency. 
- 06:35 half-open probes start: 5 probes succeed at p50 ~ 300ms but one probe times out -> circuit returns to open for additional 45s. Oscillation continues for 3 minutes before settling at 08:00.

Simple ASCII latency series (excerpt p99 premium, in ms):
- timeline (s):  0   30  60  90  120 150 180 210 240 270 300 330
- p99 (ms):     320 330 340 360 580 400 420 980 120  130  180  220

Emergent behaviour notes:
- Feedback loop hypothesis plausibility: when CB trips on premium, cheap is forced to absorb traffic; cheap saturates and latency increases which then prevents premium from recovering because the system waits for cheap to stabilize (backpressure at the ingress). In short: the fallback path becoming saturated blocks the path for controlled healing of premium.
- Another contributing factor: kv-cache priming. Premium had higher cache-hit rates; when traffic moves to cheap, cheap requests experience more cold starts that generate additional backend IO, amplifying pressure.
- CB configuration sensitivity: reducing cooldown from 45s to 20s reduced oscillation amplitude but caused more frequent open/close transitions; increasing min-premium-qps avoided complete starvation and reduced time-to-heal.

Quick quantitative table (single-run trimmed):
- metric | premium | cheap | total
- baseline p99 (steady) | "320ms" | "210ms" | "320ms"
- peak p99 (during worst burst) | "980ms" | "480ms" | "980ms"
- avg GPU util (burst window) | "48%" | "72%" | "—"
- cb-open events | "1 (major) + few short" | "n/a" | "1"

Config experiments tried (small grid):
- grid A: cooldown in {20s, 45s, 90s}, min-premium-qps in {0, 5, 10, 20}
- grid B: trip_condition alternative -> increase p99 threshold to 1s and add slope filter (detect 3-point rising trend)
- grid C: ingress backpressure -> add small reservoir queue per-model to smooth sudden reroutes (size 25 requests)

Preliminary takeaways:
- Never fully starve premium: min-premium-qps=10 prevents long recovery; set as a safety floor for customer-tiered traffic.
- Prefer slope-based trip signals: single-window p99 triggers are too noisy and cause brittle oscillation for mixed routing. 3-point rising trend filter reduced false trips in further runs.
- Implement cheap-path admission control: fallbacks need admission limits stronger than the premium pool's assumption. Without it the fallback becomes the bottleneck and prevents healing.
- Add cache-warmup hints: when traffic is fractional-routed, route initial tokens of a session to premium to prime caches then converge to cheap, or proactively seed cheap's cache in anticipation of shifts.

Planned next runs (short list):
- run-grid-1: cooldown=30s, min-premium-qps=8, slope-filter enabled; measure oscillator amplitude over 30m window.
- run-grid-2: add fallback admission limit = 40% of fallback GPU capacity; replay with 60/40 default split to force fallback pressure.
- run-grid-3: simulate sticky sessions where 20% of tenants have session affinity to premium for 60s to see cache priming effect.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do multi-tenant fairness rules interact? If multiple tenants' circuits open simultaneously for the same fallback pool, will admission control per-tenant be required?
- Can we cheaply detect kv-cache heat imbalance across model variants to trigger proactive seeding?
- Add observability metric: 'fallback-recovery-time' (time from first CB open to premium p99 returning within 1.5x baseline).

Notes to self: keep this run artifact-linked to JIRA-ENG-8342 and attach the raw replay logs. Share quick summary with Maya/Ibrahim and ask for thoughts on whether implementing per-fallback reservoir queues is feasible in the short term.

End of scratchpad.
